functions: Talking about past actions (Spreadsheets and formulae)
Explaining sequences of system administration tasks (Systems administration)
grammarFocus: Past simple for finished actions in the past; did/didn't + bare infinitive in questions and negative sentences; irregular past forms (took, found, went)
By + -ing to express how to do things: By running a query, you can find the customers in one city.
While, before, after to show the order of events; -ing form after these words when the subject is the same in both clauses, a full clause when the subject is different
Past continuous and past simple: past continuous for the longer action in progress, past simple for the shorter action that interrupts it; when + past simple, while + past continuous

parts.context: Mia, a sales manager, asks Felix, the database administrator, how to get some information from the customer database.

script.speaker: Mia
script.text: Felix, have you got a minute? The marketing team wants a list of all our customers in Da Lat who bought something last year. How can I get that from the database?

script.speaker: Felix
script.text: You can do it by running a query. Open the database, click the Create tab, and then choose Query Design.

script.speaker: Mia
script.text: OK, I've done that. Which tables do I need?

script.speaker: Felix
script.text: Just two: Customers and Orders. Add both of them. Then drag the fields you need into the grid at the bottom: Name, Email, City and Order Date.

script.speaker: Mia
script.text: Right. How do I choose only Da Lat?

script.speaker: Felix
script.text: In the City column, type Da Lat in the Criteria row. And in the Order Date column, type the dates for last year.

script.speaker: Felix
script.text: Click Run. The database finds all the matching records. By saving the query, you can run it again next year without starting from the beginning.

script.speaker: Mia
script.text: That's really useful. Can I send the list straight to Marketing?

script.speaker: Felix
script.text: Yes, by exporting it to a spreadsheet. But first, please remove the customers who don't want marketing emails. There's a field called No Marketing for that.

parts.context: Nora, a systems administrator, leaves a voice message for Kim, a colleague on the morning shift, about last night's server update.

script.speaker: Nora
script.text: Hi Kim, it's Nora. Before you start your morning shift, here's how last night's update went. I started at ten o'clock in the evening. Before installing anything, I backed up all three servers to the NAS. That took about forty minutes.

script.speaker: Nora
script.text: Then I installed the update on the mail server first, because it's the most important one. While it was installing, I checked the logs on the other two servers. There were no errors. After restarting the mail server, I sent a few test emails. Everything worked, so I moved on to the file server and the web server. I finished at half past one.

script.speaker: Nora
script.text: There was only one small problem. The web server didn't restart by itself, so I had to switch it on by hand. It's fine now.

script.speaker: Nora
script.text: Early this morning, two people from Sales couldn't open the shared drive. That wasn't because of the update. Their laptops were still connected to the guest wi-fi, so I connected them to the staff network. OK, that's everything. Bye.

questions.stem: What time did Nora start the update?
questions.explanation: "I started at ten o'clock, after everyone went home."

questions.stem: Where did Nora back up the three servers?
questions.explanation: "Before installing anything, I backed up all three servers to the NAS."

questions.stem: Which server did Nora update first?
questions.explanation: "I installed the update on the mail server first, because it's the most important one."
"I finished at half past one."

questions.stem: Which network were the two Sales laptops still connected to?
questions.explanation: "Their laptops were still connected to the guest wi-fi, so I connected them to the staff network."

definitions.text: A line of numbers or words written under each other that goes down a page.
In a table, something that uniquely identifies each record.
A situation in which a machine does not work because something is stopping a part from moving.

To organise or move equipment so that it is in the right place and ready to be used.

items.explanation: Deploy (triển khai) là sắp xếp, đưa thiết bị (hoặc phần mềm) vào đúng chỗ để sẵn sàng sử dụng.
Caps Lock (phím viết hoa) là phím bấm khi muốn gõ toàn chữ in hoa.
Touch screen (màn hình cảm ứng) là màn hình chạm vào để ra lệnh cho máy tính hoặc lấy thông tin.
Primary key (khoá chính) là thứ xác định duy nhất mỗi bản ghi trong một bảng. Định nghĩa A là của column (cột), không có trong danh sách thuật ngữ.
Jam (sự kẹt) là tình trạng máy không chạy vì có vật cản một bộ phận chuyển động, ví dụ kẹt giấy.

grammar.stem: ______ you back up the customer files yesterday?
grammar.explanation: Câu hỏi quá khứ đơn (yesterday): Did + chủ ngữ + động từ nguyên mẫu (back up).

grammar.stem: The update ______ two hours to install yesterday.
grammar.explanation: "take" là động từ bất quy tắc: quá khứ đơn là "took" (taken là quá khứ phân từ).

grammar.stem: 'How did you find the missing invoice?' '______ the database for the customer's name.'
grammar.explanation: Trả lời câu hỏi "How…?" (bằng cách nào) dùng by + V-ing: By searching…

grammar.stem: After the technician ______ the new printer, everyone could print again.
grammar.explanation: Hai vế khác chủ ngữ (the technician / everyone) nên sau "after" là một mệnh đề đầy đủ: After the technician installed… Chỉ dùng V-ing khi hai vế cùng chủ ngữ.

grammar.stem: ______ I was copying the files to the NAS, the cable came out.
grammar.explanation: Trước mệnh đề quá khứ tiếp diễn (I was updating…) dùng liên từ "While". "During" và "For" là giới từ, phải đi với danh từ, không đi với mệnh đề.

grammar.stem: The users ______ the new system when the error message appeared.
grammar.explanation: Hành động đang diễn ra trong quá khứ thì bị xen vào (when the error message appeared): quá khứ tiếp diễn; chủ ngữ số nhiều (The users) nên "were testing".

grammar.stem: When the laptop suddenly ______ off, I lost my work.
grammar.explanation: Sự việc ngắn trong quá khứ sau "when" dùng quá khứ đơn: went (quá khứ của go); go off = tắt.

vocabulary.stem: I need last March's sales figures. Can you ______ the database for me?
vocabulary.explanation: Query the database (truy vấn cơ sở dữ liệu) là đặt câu hỏi với dữ liệu đã lưu để lấy thông tin.

vocabulary.stem: The new receptionist filled in a ______ with her name, address and bank details.
vocabulary.explanation: Form (biểu mẫu) là văn bản có các ô trống để điền thông tin, nhất là thông tin cá nhân.

vocabulary.stem: Could you ______ me through the new booking system? I've never used it before.
vocabulary.explanation: Walk sb through sth (giải thích, hướng dẫn từng bước cho ai).

vocabulary.stem: The router stopped working, so I ______ it to the factory settings.
vocabulary.explanation: Reset (đặt lại) thiết bị về cài đặt gốc để dùng lại được. Quá khứ của reset vẫn là reset.

vocabulary.stem: Please ______ the new user's details carefully before you create the account.
vocabulary.explanation: Check sth out (kiểm tra kỹ xem có đúng không) trước khi tạo tài khoản.

vocabulary.stem: To find the average, add the numbers and then ______ the total by the number of items.
vocabulary.explanation: Divide (chia): muốn tính trung bình thì cộng các số rồi chia tổng cho số lượng. "subtract" không đi với "by" theo nghĩa này.

vocabulary.stem: A keyboard and a mouse are both ______ devices: they put information into a computer.
vocabulary.explanation: Input device (thiết bị đầu vào) đưa thông tin vào máy tính, ví dụ bàn phím, chuột.

vocabulary.stem: The NAS device is ______ to the office network, so everyone can save files on it.
vocabulary.explanation: Attached (được gắn, nối vào) cái gì: thiết bị NAS nối vào mạng văn phòng.

passage.title: Incident Report: Ticket Machines at Riverside Cinema
paragraphs: On Saturday 12th October, the six self-service ticket machines at Riverside Cinema stopped taking card payments for almost two hours. This report explains what happened and what we did.

At 6.40 p.m., the cinema was very busy. About forty customers were buying tickets for the seven o'clock films when the card readers on all six machines suddenly stopped working. Each machine showed the message 'Payment service not available'. While the duty manager was calling the IT helpdesk, staff opened two extra counters and sold tickets by hand.

The technician, Sam Ortiz, connected to the machines from his office. After checking the system logs, he found the cause. The night before, the payment company had installed a software update on all the card readers. The update had a bug, and it stopped the readers when there were more than ten payments in one minute.

Sam could not remove the update himself, so he phoned the payment company. Their engineer removed it at 8.30 p.m., and the machines worked normally again. Two films started fifteen minutes late, and the cinema gave free drinks to about 200 customers.

In future, the payment company will test every update on one machine for a week before installing it on the others. The cinema will also keep a portable card reader at the main counter, so that staff can sell tickets quickly if the machines stop again.

passage.title: Problems with the September sales report
paragraphs: Last week, the monthly sales report showed that we sold £86,000 of goods in September. This number looked too high, so Karen in Finance checked the spreadsheet on Monday.

She found two problems. First, someone copied some of the October sales into the September sheet. Second, the formula in the Total column added the tax twice. Karen corrected both problems, and the real total for September was £71,500.

Before sending the report again, she asked Tom to check all the other formulae. While he was checking them, he found another small error in the Returns column, but it did not change the total. Karen then sent the corrected report to the directors on Tuesday afternoon.

To stop these problems in future, we are going to protect all the cells with formulae, so that only the finance team can change them. Please don't copy data into the report by hand any more. From next month, the report will take the numbers directly from the sales database.

email.task:
You are a support technician. Daisy, a new receptionist, often uses the office printer, and this morning the paper got stuck inside it. Write an email to Daisy explaining how to clear a paper jam, using the notes below. In your email you must use:
- before or after + -ing at least twice to show the order of the steps (Before opening…, After removing…);
- by + -ing at least once to explain how to do something (by looking…).
Follow the standard layout for an email giving instructions: From / To / Date / Subject, a greeting, It should be quite easy to …, the steps with First / Then / Next / After that / Finally, a reminder (Don't forget to … when you've finished.), then Best wishes and your name, position and department.
Write 80–100 words (do not count the From, To, Date and Subject lines).
bullets: switch off the printer / unplug it (before opening the cover)
open the front cover / take out the paper tray
pull the stuck paper out slowly with both hands
check for small pieces of paper: look inside with a torch
put the tray back / close the cover
plug the printer in / print a test page
reminder: wash your hands when you've finished
targetGrammar: Before / after + -ing (at least twice): Before opening the cover, switch off…; After removing the paper, check…
By + -ing (at least once): check for small pieces by looking inside with a torch
Imperatives with sequence words for the steps
email.modelAnswer:
From: Do Thanh Tam
To: Daisy
Date: 21st January
Subject: Clearing a paper jam

Hi Daisy,

It should be quite easy to clear a paper jam.
First, before opening the cover, switch off the printer and unplug it.
Then, open the front cover and take out the paper tray.
Next, just pull the stuck paper out slowly with both hands.
After that, check for small pieces of paper by looking inside with a torch.
Finally, after putting the tray back and closing the cover, plug the printer in and print a test page.
Don't forget to wash your hands when you've finished.

Best wishes,
Do Thanh Tam
Support Technician
Help Desk Department

parts.instructions: Answer the three questions. Speak for 30–45 seconds for each question.
questions: Tell me about the first computer or phone you had. When did you get it, and what did you use it for? Use the past simple.
What do you do before starting and after finishing an assignment on a computer? Use before + -ing and after + -ing (Before starting…, After finishing…).
What were you doing at eight o'clock yesterday evening? Did anything interrupt you? Use the past continuous and the past simple (I was …ing when …).

parts.instructions: Talk about a spreadsheet you made. Speak for 1–1.5 minutes.
parts.prompt: Last term you made a spreadsheet to follow your marks in one subject. Explain what you did and which formulae you used. Use the past simple (I made…, I typed…, I divided…) and spreadsheet words such as column, row, cell, minus, divide and brackets.
cues: one row for each test, one column for each part of the test
the marks for the three parts of each test in columns B, C and D
column E: (B+C+D) divided by three, with brackets, for the average
column F: the target mark minus the average
the cell turned green when the average was higher than the target
requiredGrammar: Past simple for finished actions: I made…, I typed…, I divided…
Spreadsheet language: column, row, cell, minus, divide, brackets
parts.sampleAnswer: Last term, I made a spreadsheet for my maths marks. I used one row for each test, and the three parts of each test were in columns B, C and D. In column E, I typed a formula with brackets: B plus C plus D in brackets, divided by three. The brackets were important, because without them the spreadsheet divided only D by three. That gave me the average for each test. Then, in column F, I wrote my target mark minus the average, so I could see how many marks I needed. I also made the cell turn green when the average was higher than the target. By the end of the term, most of the cells were green, and I felt much more confident.

parts.instructions: Deal with the situation. Speak for 1–1.5 minutes.
parts.prompt: Yesterday a new colleague, Lan, could not log in to her account. A colleague from another office phones you and asks what happened. Use the cues to explain how the problem occurred and what you did. Use the past continuous for the actions in progress and the past simple for what happened (She was …ing when …; While I was …ing, …).
cues: 9.30 a.m.: Lan / prepare the monthly report
her laptop / restart for an update → she / log in again
Caps Lock / be on → she / type the wrong password three times → the system / lock her out
while you / reset her password → she / use a colleague's laptop
after resetting it → you / show her the Caps Lock light
requiredGrammar: Past continuous for the longer action: She was preparing…, While I was resetting…
Past simple for the shorter action and for what you did: the laptop restarted, the system locked her out, I showed…
parts.sampleAnswer: Yesterday morning, at about half past nine, Lan was preparing the monthly report when her laptop suddenly restarted for an update. When it came back on, she tried to log in again. Unfortunately, the Caps Lock was on, but she didn't notice it. She typed her password three times, and each time it was wrong, so the system locked her out of her account. She phoned me, and I went to her desk. While I was resetting her password, she used a colleague's laptop, so she didn't lose too much time. After resetting it, I showed her the small Caps Lock light on the keyboard. She logged in with the new password at about ten o'clock and finished the report before lunch.
